data.title: HCLTech (NSE:HCLTECH) heads into Monday with revenue focus after $1.14 billion AI contract
data.description:
Mumbai, July 6, 2026, 03:35 IST

  • Cash equities in India haven’t opened yet ahead of the 09:15 IST start. HCLTech was last at ₹1,140 on the NSE on July 3, gaining 5.74%.
  • The deal makes up around 12% of HCLTech’s projected FY26 new-deal wins. Spread out across 5-1/2 years, it accounts for roughly 1.4% of the company’s FY26 revenue.
  • HCLTech’s board will meet July 13 to review Q1 FY27 numbers and take up a possible dividend.

HCL Technologies Limited (NSE:HCLTECH) heads into Monday with a big new AI deal, but the stock’s move on Friday shows the market is still waiting on the June-quarter numbers. NSE normal trading hours are 09:15 to 15:30 IST, so Friday’s close is the latest official price. HCLTech’s investor site listed the stock at ₹1,140 on the NSE, up ₹61.90, or 5.74%, on July 3.

HCLTech has picked up a $1.14 billion deal with a top European firm, Reuters said. The Noida IT group will build an AI-backed operating model for the client’s digital workplace and enterprise networks. The contract lasts five-and-a-half years, with an option to extend for another five, and the business is all-new for HCLTech. It’s the company’s biggest announced deal since it signed a $2.1 billion contract with Verizon in August 2023.

HCLTech kept the client name under wraps. But The Economic Times reported, citing sources, that the client is Mercedes-Benz Group AG (ETR:MBG). The paper also said HCLTech won out over Infosys Limited (NSE:INFY), which previously held the account. Mercedes-Benz told ET it “does not comment on deal specifics”. The Economic Times

The scale isn’t so clear. Spanning 66 months, the deal is roughly $207 million per year. That’s 1.4% of HCLTech’s projected FY26 dollar revenue. It makes up 12.2% of the FY26 new-deal total contract value, based on the company’s own numbers.

The numbers are important because HCLTech’s FY27 outlook is still tight: 1%-4% constant-currency revenue growth, 1.5%-4.5% services revenue growth, and EBIT margin at 17.5%-18.5%. A solid ramp supports the guidance, but doesn’t automatically raise the full-year growth base.

HCLTech CEO C. Vijayakumar said in April the company’s “AI-led service offerings are getting traction,” with Advanced AI annualised revenue topping $620 million in Q4. Now, July 13 commentary will focus more on how quickly the European deal ramps up and its contribution to AI revenue, rather than just the total contract value. HCLTech

HCLTech jumped 5.74% on Friday, far outpacing sector peers. Infosys added 0.60%, Wipro Limited (NSE:WIPRO) climbed 1.01%, and Tata Consultancy Services Limited (NSE:TCS) rose 1.24%. Sensex ended up 0.34%, Nifty 50 gained 0.39%, and the Nifty IT index was up 1.8%.

Market cap for HCL Technologies stood at ₹309,086 crore, according to Economic Times, after shares rose ₹60.91 on Friday. That move tacked on about ₹16,500 crore in value for the day. Despite the bounce, the stock is still off 18.77% over three months and down 33.47% over the past year, by the same data.

The gap shows why the sector’s so sensitive. Back in April, HCLTech dropped 10.8%—its biggest fall in over a decade—after its weak annual growth outlook dragged IT stocks down. Bajaj Broking’s Shashwat Singh said at the time that concerns about near-term demand and growth visibility were weighing on the group. Friday’s order answers some of those concerns, but not all.

Another AI-data headline came up last week. HCLTech’s investor page showed that HCLSoftware closed the Jaspersoft buy on July 2. When they first announced it, Marc Potter, CEO of Actian and general manager for HCLSoftware’s Data & AI division, said customers want BI tools that offer “consistent analytics and reports”. HCLSoftware posted ARR of $1.05 billion in FY26, off 0.5% in constant currency. HCLTech

Analyst calls haven’t shifted to a clear buy yet. MarketScreener lists a HOLD call from 40 analysts, with an average target of ₹1,309.82—roughly 15% higher than Friday’s close.

The board meets July 13 to sign off on unaudited results for the quarter to June 30 and to review a possible second interim dividend for FY27. The main issue is how much of the new deal lands in FY27 revenue, and if management sticks with its 1%-4% constant-currency revenue target.

data.title: Hang Seng Edges Up After AI Selloff; Rate Worries, China Growth Uncertainty Linger
data.description:
Hong Kong, June 15, 2026, 16:57 (HKT).

  • Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong rose 124 points, or 0.5%, to finish at 24,842 on Monday. The Hang Seng Tech Index gained 1.3% to 4,765.
  • Stocks bounced after a steep drop last week, which saw five days of losses and the market falling close to late-March lows.
  • Traders look to the US-Iran deal, oil prices, the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting, and weak credit demand in China for direction.

Hong Kong shares bounced Monday as regional sentiment picked up after the US and Iran reached a deal to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Hang Seng Index finished 124 points higher at 24,842. Turnover came in at HK$283.35 billion. The Hang Seng China Enterprises Index was little changed at 8,375. The Hang Seng Tech Index added 60 points to 4,765. SMIC jumped 7% to HK$76.65. Knowledge Atlas soared 32.8%. Tencent and Alibaba both ended in the red, even as turnover stayed heavy.

Hang Seng’s rebound doesn’t make up for last week’s slide. By Tuesday, the index had dropped for five days, ending near 24,566 as shares in finance, retail and energy lost ground. Investors grew wary of China’s recovery. Losses accelerated by Thursday, when the Hang Seng hit 24,249, the lowest since July 2025, then bounced Friday.

Stocks dropped earlier as traders pulled back from popular AI names and worried that hot US data could mean rates stay higher. The South China Morning Post reported that Hong Kong stocks slid on June 8, tracking other Asian markets lower after a US jobs report fired up fresh rate-hike fears. Charu Chanana at Saxo called the move “not a full-blown panic,” but said it was a repricing after a sharp run-up in AI-related stocks. South China Morning Post

Oil’s drop and a softer dollar triggered Monday’s bounce, giving markets a break. Brent crude lost about 5% to $82.9 a barrel after Reuters said the US-Iran framework was in play, while risk assets picked up. The deal isn’t final yet. “There’s plenty of room to be disappointed here,” said Nick Rees at Monex Europe, with investors still looking for clarity on Iran’s nuclear plans. Reuters

Hong Kong stocks face a new test as traders look to see if the rally spreads past semiconductor and AI-related shares. According to a Reuters piece published by Business Recorder, the tech sector in Hong Kong was up 6% at midday, while consumer and property names lagged. The report also said that China’s May bank lending missed estimates, showing that the property slump is still holding back household demand for loans.

Technical traders are still wary here. The Hang Seng dropped under its 50-day exponential moving average, a key trend marker. One Invezz analysis picked up by CryptoRank pointed to 24,400 as critical support, with 24,000 below that if things worsen. The index did finish above 24,800 on Monday, which helps in the short term, but bigger risks remain. Hong Kong stocks are still moving on Fed signals, oil swings and doubts on whether China’s economy can manage more than just an AI-driven bounce.

data.title: HDFC Bank stock edges higher after Q1 loan growth, time-deposit growth slows
data.description:
MUMBAI, July 6, 2026, 13:51 IST

  • HDFC Bank was up 3.57% at ₹829.70 at 13:34 IST, just off its session high of ₹831.
  • Gross advances were up 15.4% from a year ago, while deposits climbed 14.7%.
  • The bank’s provisional data show time deposits accounted for roughly 78% of the increase in deposits from a year earlier.
  • Piran Engineer at CLSA said most banks’ provisional numbers “met or exceeded our estimates.” Reuters

HDFC Bank Limited (NSE:HDFCBANK) surged Monday after its June-quarter numbers put loan growth back in focus for investors. The shares were at ₹829.70, up ₹28.65, as of 13:34 IST, opening at ₹805 versus Friday’s ₹801.05 close. Still, the stock is down 19.37% over one year, so the move was a partial bounce rather than a full comeback.

Advances was the key number. The bank said gross advances at period-end reached ₹30.61 trillion as of June 30, up from ₹26.53 trillion last year. Deposits climbed to ₹31.71 trillion from ₹27.64 trillion. The funding mix was weaker—time deposits saw faster growth than current and savings accounts.

The margin pressure is visible underneath the top-line number. Period-end CASA deposits made up 32.3% of total deposits, falling from 33.9% last year and 34.1% at March-end, based on the bank’s update. Of the ₹4.06 trillion rise in deposits over the year, time deposits accounted for ₹3.18 trillion. CASA brought in ₹0.89 trillion.

The market’s opening move could still depend on net interest margin numbers. CLSA senior research analyst Engineer said that banks’ provisional figures mostly “met or exceeded our estimates,” but pointed out the “potential impact of declining CASA ratios on margins” as something to watch. Reuters

Business Standard said Motilal Oswal analysts expect HDFC Bank’s credit-deposit ratio to go up to 95.8% from 94.6% last quarter, with margins narrowing by about 2 basis points. ICICI Securities noted advances and deposits kept growing, but CASA slipped a bit from the last quarter.

Private banks reported fresh numbers for the quarter, giving traders a point of comparison. Axis Bank Limited (NSE:AXISBANK) traded higher after it posted an 18.8% jump in gross advances. Kotak Mahindra Bank Limited (NSE:KOTAKBANK) slipped as its growth came in softer.

HDFC Bank is set to report June-quarter numbers on July 18. Its latest update didn’t include any figures for profit, margin, slippages, or loan yields. Investors will focus on what management says about asset quality and growth plans.

data.title: Sumitomo Chemical India (NSE:SUMICHEM) 14% jump puts crop-chem stock on chip-news valuation watch
data.description:
BENGALURU, July 6, 2026, 02:41 IST

  • Sumitomo Chemical India closed at ₹502.30 on Friday, up 13.85%, with 29.49 million NSE shares traded.
  • Friday accounted for 92.6% of last week’s share volume, based on daily market data.
  • Parent Sumitomo Chemical Co. (TYO:4005) named its Korean unit, not the India listed arm, in a Samsung glass-core substrate venture.
  • The stock closed at about 46 times FY26 consolidated profit, while current monsoon conditions keep crop-chemical demand in view.

Sumitomo Chemical India Ltd. (NSE:SUMICHEM) heads into Monday’s open after a one-day rally that looked more like a parent-linked semiconductor repricing than a read-through from its own agrochemical earnings. The stock rose 13.85% on Friday to ₹502.30, its best recent close after heavy volume, while NSE data put the day’s turnover at 29.49 million shares.

At the dateline time, regular NSE equity trading had not started; the exchange lists normal trading at 09:15 to 15:30 IST, and its 2026 equity holiday list does not show July 6 as a trading holiday.

The week’s tape was lopsided. Friday made up 92.6% of the five-session volume, and the day’s ₹61.10 price rise was about 91% of the stock’s one-week absolute gain from the June 25 close.

The buying followed a July 2 release from Sumitomo Chemical Co. (TYO:4005), which said wholly owned Korean subsidiary Dongwoo Fine-Chem had signed a joint venture agreement with Samsung Electro-Mechanics Co. (KRX:009150) to make glass core substrates for advanced semiconductor packages. The planned venture, GlaSSEM, will have share capital of KRW 482.1 billion, with Samsung Electro-Mechanics owning 66% and Dongwoo Fine-Chem 34%; the release names Dongwoo and Samsung as the investing companies and does not name Sumitomo Chemical India as a party to the venture.

That distinction matters for investors because the India-listed company’s own earnings base is still crop protection. Its FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was ₹3,238.3 crore and profit for the year was ₹543.0 crore, according to its financial filing.

Managing Director Chetan Shah told investors on May 28 that FY26 was “one of the most challenging years” for the Indian agrochemical industry, citing long and excess rainfall through the peak kharif consumption period. He also said the company delivered ₹543 crore profit after tax, a gross profit margin of 42% and an EBITDA margin of 20.7%.

The company’s annual report gave the same weather link in plainer operating terms: excess and prolonged rainfall from July to September, stretching into October in some regions, damaged soybean, cotton and groundnut crops and cut spray opportunities during critical application windows.

The next test is not chip substrates. India’s weather office warned on Sunday of heavy to very heavy rain with isolated extremely heavy rain on July 6 over Chhattisgarh, Gujarat Region, Konkan & Goa and Madhya Maharashtra, among other areas. For crop-chemical makers, heavy rain can raise pest and disease risk, but it can also delay spraying, the same issue Sumitomo Chemical India cited for FY26.

The wider Indian market gave little cover for the size of Friday’s stock move. The Sensex rose 0.34% and the Nifty 50 gained 0.39% on Friday, while both were up about 0.9% for the week. Sat Duhra, portfolio manager at Janus Henderson, told Reuters the Indian market still “needs a strong earnings pulse.” Reuters

The next dated company events are mechanical but still relevant after a 14% rally. Sumitomo Chemical India has fixed July 17 as the record date for a ₹1.30 per-share dividend, equal to about 0.26% of Friday’s close, and its annual general meeting is scheduled for July 27.

data.title: India week ahead: TCS results on tap, monsoon worries linger
data.description:
BENGALURU, July 6, 2026, 04:32 (IST)

  • Nifty 50 (INDEXNSE:NIFTY_50) finished Friday at 24,270.85, gaining around 0.9% for the week. The BSE Sensex (INDEXBOM:SENSEX) settled at 77,763.91.
  • Foreign institutional investors offloaded 4,004 crore rupees net in cash stocks last week. Domestic funds stepped up and bought 12,634 crore rupees, over triple the FIIs’ outflow, according to .
  • Tata Consultancy Services (NSE:TCS) is set to report June-quarter results on July 9. This is the first major earnings test for the Nifty IT recovery.
  • Rain worries for July remain after the IMD put out a forecast for rainfall below 94% of the long-period average.

Indian stocks head into the week trading less than 1% under 24,500, a level technical analysts keep an eye on. Markets climbed last week, but the gains leaned on local buying more than foreign flows. NSE’s regular cash market opens at 9:15 a.m. IST. The 2026 equity holiday schedule skips July 6, so there’s no break just after Muharram on June 26.

Stocks rose again last week with the Nifty 50 and Sensex up around 0.9%, marking a fourth straight week of gains as oil prices fell and the latest U.S. jobs report came in soft. The Nifty IT index climbed 1.8% on Friday, breaking its five-week losing streak, according to Reuters. Sat Duhra from Janus Henderson Investors said the RBI’s moves had given markets “breathing room,” but said Indian stocks still lack a “strong earnings pulse.” Reuters

The flow split is the focus. Foreign funds were net sellers in four out of five sessions, stepping in to buy on Friday. Domestic funds took the other side through Thursday, then turned sellers Friday. That rotation stands out with the index at resistance and foreign appetite uneven for now.

TCS is the first major test for stocks. ETMarkets reported that India’s top IT services firm will post April-June results on July 9, kicking off earnings for large-cap IT. Siddhartha Khemka, research head for wealth management at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said the Nifty IT move was driven by value buying and a pickup in global tech sentiment.

Oil is the second major data point. OPEC+ gave the green light for another 188,000 barrels per day in output from August. Reuters reported oil prices hovered near $72 a barrel after Hormuz exports restarted. That helps take some pressure off the rupee and margins for India’s energy, but if oil bounces back, oil marketing, paint, tyre, and airline stocks get hit.

Monsoon risk isn’t easing this year. The government’s May 29 forecast pegged the 2026 southwest monsoon at just 90% of the long-period average, and said there’s an 84% chance of below-normal or worse rainfall. Business Standard said the weather office now sees July rain slipping below 94% of the LPA.

That leaves rural demand shares tough to price. A couple of solid days for autos, lenders or staples doesn’t clear things up. Next up is the CPI data on July 13, with the release expected to get attention for signs of food-price pressure. MoSPI said June CPI comes out that day.

Corporate actions are adding noise to single-stock trading. ETMarkets said 49 firms have record dates this week. Names include JSW Steel (NSE:JSWSTEEL), Sun Pharmaceutical Industries (NSE:SUNPHARMA), Titan Company (NSE:TITAN), Axis Bank (NSE:AXISBANK), BSE Ltd (NSE:BSE) and Nestle India (NSE:NESTLEIND). Friday has 29 record-date companies on the list, the most of any day.

Vinod Nair, research head at Geojit Investments, said near-term moves would depend on earnings, how the monsoon goes, credit growth and what happens in trade talks. Jateen Trivedi at LKP Securities pegged the rupee’s range between 95.00 and 95.45 per dollar. Rupak De at LKP said Nifty has support first at 24,200, then at 24,000, with the next resistance at 24,500.

The main question this week is if Friday’s FII buying marks a shift or was just a blip. Another day of foreign inflows but with less help from domestic funds could push the market to retest 24,500. If FIIs go back to selling, the pressure lands on locals again ahead of TCS earnings.

data.title: Eicher Motors falls as Delhi’s EV rules pressure Royal Enfield bikes
data.description:
BENGALURU, June 30, 2026, 22:40 IST

  • Eicher Motors ended down 4.75% at ₹7,073.50. The Nifty 50 dipped 0.34%, while the Sensex was off 0.33%.
  • Delhi’s new EV Policy 2026-2030 starts on July 1. The plan will ban new petrol and CNG two-wheeler registrations starting April 1, 2028.
  • Royal Enfield reported 91% of its May sales in the domestic market, with 88% from models up to 350cc, according to data from Eicher.
  • Ather Energy and Ola Electric moved higher after investors bought into listed EV two-wheeler stocks.

Eicher Motors Limited (NSE:EICHERMOT) fell sharply Tuesday, dropping 4.75% to close at ₹7,073.50. The stock sold off harder than expected after the one-city policy news, making it one of the top losers on The Economic Times screen. It hit a low of ₹6,942.50 during the session, down 6.5% from Monday. ET data shows that only 2.11% of Eicher’s sessions over the last 21 years have seen intraday drops greater than 5%.

The drop wiped out about ₹9,700 crore in equity value, based on ET’s market cap figure of ₹194,036 crore at Tuesday’s close and the day’s loss. The Nifty 50 closed down 0.34% at 23,865.75, while the Sensex dropped 0.33% to 76,478.67. Eicher’s move was more than just a drag on the index.

Delhi’s cabinet signed off on an EV policy running through March 31, 2030, with an outlay of ₹15,000 crore. The policy stops registrations of new auto-rickshaws that aren’t electric from Jan. 1, 2027, and no new non-electric two-wheelers from April 1, 2028. Business Standard reported that automakers came under pressure on fears other states may adopt similar rules.

Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services, told Business Today this policy is raising worries about the “long-term demand outlook” for Royal Enfield motorcycles. Nomura said Royal Enfield could get hit harder because it has “higher Delhi exposure and very low EV mix potential.” Kranthi Bathini, director of equity strategy at WealthMills Securities, said there’s profit booking in the stock and fresh buyers might want to “buy on dips.” Business Today

Royal Enfield’s May sales were up 15% at 103,231 bikes, Eicher said in its June 1 update. The main contributor was domestic bikes up to 350cc. Exports dropped 33%. Sales of bikes over 350cc fell 4%. Headline growth did not show the full picture.

The split helps explain how a Delhi rule landed on a national stock. New data showed Eicher’s bike demand stuck mostly to India and still relying on petrol-powered 350cc-heavy Royal Enfield models. In the same month, the offsets got slimmer: exports fell, and demand for bigger bikes also dropped.

Eicher’s CV business posted stronger May numbers, but the stock didn’t move on it. VE Commercial Vehicles said total sales for May were 7,978 units, rising 7.8%, as domestic sales climbed 9.1%. Exports dropped 17.2%.

B. Govindarajan, who runs Eicher Motors as managing director and heads Royal Enfield, said in the May update the company saw “continued growth in Q1” even with macro headwinds. He pointed to the Bullet 650 launch and said there are plans for a new manufacturing plant in Andhra Pradesh. In the same update, the company said Royal Enfield has now introduced its first electric motorcycle, the FF.C6, under the Flying Flea name.

The listed EV side traded more clearly. Ather Energy CEO Tarun Mehta said Delhi’s mix of incentives, mandates and charging infrastructure built a “strong foundation.” Ather shares gained more than 5% at one point, hitting a new 52-week high. Ola Electric jumped over 11%, ET reported. The Economic Times

Eicher started Tuesday with a solid earnings track, more than most auto bears would want to short. Reuters said in May that Eicher’s March-quarter net profit jumped nearly 12% to ₹15.2 billion and sales climbed 16% to ₹60.80 billion, beating analyst numbers from LSEG. Tuesday’s drop in the stock put policy risk in focus above those earnings.

data.title: Bharti Airtel (NSE:BHARTIARTL) up as subscriber growth leads market in May
data.description:
MUMBAI, July 1, 2026, 01:34 IST

  • Bharti Airtel closed Tuesday at ₹1,852.00, gaining 0.59%. Shares hit ₹1,876.60 at the session high. The Nifty 50 dropped 0.34%, while the Sensex was down 0.33%.
  • Airtel captured 57.5% of wireless-mobile net adds in May, with its share of the market at 37.89%, according to TRAI data.
  • Nomura lifted its price target on Airtel to ₹2,355, 27.2% above where the stock ended on Tuesday, naming it the firm’s top pick in the telecom sector.
  • The stock sits 14.8% under its 52-week high. Nomura’s target is 8.3% higher than that high.

Bharti Airtel Limited (NSE:BHARTIARTL) gained on Tuesday, bucking a soft session for Indian stocks after Nomura raised its target and new regulator numbers showed the company took a much larger chunk of May wireless-mobile net adds than its current share.

The stock finished at ₹1,852.00, up 0.59%. Shares hit an intraday high of ₹1,876.60, up 1.93%, but settled 1.31% under that level. Trading volume was 7.23 million shares, less than Monday’s 10.94 million.

The index beat was 0.93 percentage point over the Nifty 50 and 0.92 point over the Sensex. That’s notable since the stock isn’t acting like a broad-market tracker. The day was all about tariffs and subscriber moves.

TRAI’s May numbers, out last week, show Airtel picked up 2.93 million wireless-mobile subscribers in the month, beating Reliance Jio. Jio, the telecom unit of Reliance Industries (NSE:RELIANCE), added 2.15 million. Airtel’s total wireless-mobile market share sat at 37.89% by May end, still below Jio’s 39.27%, but Airtel grabbed 57.5% of May’s net new users. Vodafone Idea Limited (NSE:IDEA) added 121,289 subscribers.

The TRAI data shows Airtel led with 80.83 million M2M cellular mobile connections by end-May, grabbing a 61.65% share. Jio stood at 25.10 million connections, or 19.14%. Vodafone Idea had 21.00 million lines, giving it a 16.02% share.

Nomura raised its target for Airtel to ₹2,355, up from ₹2,220, and kept its Buy call. The firm sees Airtel delivering around 14% EBITDA and operating free cash flow CAGR for FY26-FY29, while India mobility ARPU CAGR could be close to 9%. Nomura said a tariff hike is likely in the third quarter of FY27.

Nomura is direct on valuation. The firm said Airtel’s India telecom arm trades at about 9.3 times FY28 EV/EBITDA, while Jio is at nearly 12.2 times. Airtel still leads on ARPU, margins, and free cash flow.

That’s a tough ask for a stock still off around 12% in 2026 and 14.8% under its 52-week top. Nomura’s price target is 27.2% higher than Tuesday’s close, and 8.3% above Airtel’s 52-week high of ₹2,174.50.

S&P Global Ratings lifted Airtel to BBB+ from BBB on June 24, projecting 3%-4% subscriber growth and 5%-7% ARPU gains in India over the next year. The agency also sees consolidated EBITDA up 8%-10% per year for the next two years, after jumping 28% in fiscal 2026. Rediff Credit data offers some support for the bull case.

Airtel’s data-centre plans got some new local backing. Bharti Enterprises Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal told Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy on Tuesday that Airtel is looking at Hyderabad for a second headquarters and is open to boosting data-centre capacity and fibre connectivity in the state, according to a statement in the Times of India.

Nomura points to ownership as the bigger near-term risk, not tariffs. The firm notes that Airtel’s foreign institutional investor holding sits at 28%, which could be a problem during global selloffs even if the company’s performance stays steady.

data.title: HCL Technologies (NSE:HCLTECH) soars after $1.14 billion AI contract win
data.description:
BENGALURU, July 3, 2026, 22:34 IST

  • HCLTech gained 5.74% to ₹1,140 on NSE after landing a $1.14 billion contract in Europe.
  • The straight-line yearly value comes to about $207 million, near 1.4% of FY26 revenue.
  • Nifty IT added 1.8%. HCLTech traded 12.77 million shares, roughly 3.5x its usual volume.

HCL Technologies Limited, trading as HCLTech (NSE:HCLTECH), jumped 5.74% to ₹1,140 on Friday on the NSE. The company said it picked up a $1.14 billion contract from a Fortune Global 50 firm based in Europe for an AI-powered workplace and network model. Shares reached ₹1,159 during the session, and volume hit 12.77 million shares, well above the 3.65 million average.

The contract starts in July 2026 and ends in December 2031, with an option to extend for five more years. HCLTech called it net new business, not a renewal, and did not say who the customer is.

HCLTech surged on Friday, beating out bigger IT rivals by a large margin in MarketWatch data for BSE shares. Tech Mahindra dropped.

The math tells the real story. An even split puts the contract at around $207 million a year over 5-1/2 years. That’s not much compared to HCLTech’s $14.66 billion in FY26 revenue, but it stands out against recent bookings. It’s roughly 59% of Q4 FY26 new deal wins and 12% of the full year’s new deals.

The market wasn’t just reacting to one order. HCLTech saw $4.5 billion wiped from its value in April when a weak FY27 outlook brought fresh concern about demand for India’s $315 billion IT industry. Goldman Sachs said at the time the whole sector was under pressure, with companies holding back on discretionary spends and new projects off to a slow start.

Chief Executive C Vijayakumar blamed HCLTech’s March-quarter miss on “lower discretionary spend and delayed decision making.” He said the company’s annualized Advanced AI revenue topped $620 million in Q4. For FY27, Vijayakumar said the company will focus on AI opportunities. HCLTech

HCLTech hasn’t provided margin numbers for the new contract. Mint, citing people familiar, said the contract margin is under HCLTech’s 17.2% FY26 operating margin.

“The deal also boosts HCLTech’s credibility in big competitive deals,” Phil Fersht, CEO of HFS Research, told Mint. Mint said the contract could be linked to Mercedes-Benz Group (ETR:MBG), which Infosys (NSE:INFY) has handled before. HCLTech and the client did not identify each other in the filing. mint

Better action in IT. Reuters said Nifty IT bounced 1.8% Friday, snapping a five-week drop with a 0.4% weekly gain. The Nifty 50 closed up 0.39% at 24,270.85, and the Sensex added 0.34% to 77,763.91.

HCLTech’s board will review June-quarter earnings and a second interim dividend at its meeting on July 13, per an exchange filing.

data.title: Vedanta Oil and Gas (NSE:VOGL) trades heavy after Q1 output dip, 6x jump in volumes
data.description:
Mumbai, July 4, 2026, 00:34 (IST)

  • Vedanta Oil and Gas Limited (NSE:VOGL) closed Friday at about ₹42.8, down nearly 4%. The stock had hit ₹47.60 earlier in the session. Trading volume reached 275.92 million shares, or roughly 6.3 times its usual average, data from Google Finance showed.
  • Gross operated output dropped 17% year over year to 77.7 kboepd in Q1 FY27. Working-interest output was down 16% at 51.1 kboepd.
  • Indian benchmarks climbed on Friday and ended higher for the week, but VOGL dropped while the broader market gained.

Indian stock markets are closed for the weekend. Next week, Vedanta Oil and Gas Limited (NSE:VOGL) will be in focus. The stock, which is newly listed, faces a key test: will the demerger rally last after the first production update as a standalone company showed output fell?

Shares closed Friday at ₹42.8, down 4%, after dropping about 10% from the high of the day. Google Finance put trading volume at 275.92 million shares, much higher than the 43.92 million average. Trading picked up fast after a jump and the stock recently exited trade-to-trade curbs that had blocked intraday trades.

Sources are Google Finance, Kotak Neo, and Reuters.

The stock move is important because the market is now valuing the company as a straight exploration and production play. The old conglomerate discount argument doesn’t have as much traction once new operating numbers are out.

Vedanta Oil & Gas reported Friday that average daily gross operated production came in at 77.7 kboepd for Q1 FY27, dropping from 93.2 kboepd in the same quarter last year and down from 81.5 kboepd in Q4 FY26. Working-interest output was 51.1 kboepd, compared with 60.8 kboepd a year before.

Source: company production release.

Rajasthan was the main driver here, with 63.1 kboepd out of the 77.7 kboepd gross operated output, around 81%. That’s down 15% from last year. Cambay was up 21% quarter-on-quarter, but at 4.6 kboepd, it barely made a dent against Rajasthan’s fall.

The company was direct: “Arresting Base decline and building future growth funnel.” It said it will boost output with enhanced oil recovery and more drilling.

Brokers are looking past Q1 results. Yes Securities said after the analyst meet that management laid out six business units. PL Capital told Moneycontrol the company is targeting a jump in production from around 88 kboe/d in FY26 to 150 kboe/d by FY29, wants to cut opex to $10-$13 per barrel from $16.5, and is aiming for EBITDA to grow from $492 million to $961 million.

Sources: company production release, Moneycontrol report on brokerages.

That gap means next week’s trade might focus less on Friday’s fall and more on how investors see execution risk. “I would wait for a couple of quarters before making any serious investment call,” Kranthi Bathini, director of equity strategy at WealthMills Securities, told Business Today. Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services, said new buyers should “avoid chasing the rally.” Business Today

Peer numbers give a split picture on trailing screens. Kotak Neo puts VOGL’s market value around ₹16,733 crore with a negative P/E. That’s different from Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (NSE:ONGC) and Oil India Limited (NSE:OIL), both of which have positive P/E ratios among state-run names.

Source: Peer table from Kotak Neo.

Risk appetite got a lift from the broader market last week. Reuters said the Sensex was up 0.34% at 77,763.91 on Friday and the Nifty 50 added 0.39% to 24,270.85. Both indexes finished the week higher by about 0.9%. Reuters noted Brent crude traded around $72 a barrel—a number that matters for oil producers with earnings closely tied to crude prices, according to brokers.

Vedanta Oil & Gas is starting the week with balance-sheet backing. The company said on June 29 that ICRA gave its long-term fund-based term loan an ICRA AA+ stable rating.

The upcoming local session will give the first full market look at the production release. Nifty Indices’ 2026 calendar doesn’t show any equity market holiday between the June 26 Muharram break and Sept. 14. The Cambay block dispute is still before the courts, with the company saying the Delhi High Court ordered status quo on Jan. 6, letting it run the block while the case is ongoing.

data.title: RBI fraud refunds limit bank losses, test digital banks
data.description:
MUMBAI, June 26, 2026, 14:33 IST

  • Starting Jan. 1, 2027, RBI will let eligible victims of small digital banking frauds claim up to ₹25,000 once in their lifetime.
  • For capped domestic cases, RBI covers ₹19,118 of the ₹25,000 payout, while the customer’s bank and the beneficiary bank each pay ₹2,941.
  • Banks have to do a shadow reversal for credit-card fraud complaints within five calendar days after customers report them.
  • NSE and BSE stayed closed on Friday for Muharram, so any move in local bank stocks will show up Monday.

RBI is taking on most of the direct cash cost for its small-fraud refund plan, which may shield major banks like State Bank of India (NSE:SBIN), HDFC Bank Ltd (NSE:HDFCBANK), ICICI Bank Ltd (NSE:ICICIBANK), Axis Bank Ltd (NSE:AXISBANK) and Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd (NSE:KOTAKBANK) from an immediate earnings hit. The bigger challenge for lenders is on the operations side—speeding up card refunds, lowering alert triggers and fixing complaint tracking ahead of a 2027 rollout.

The RBI has put out its final Commercial Banks – Responsible Business Conduct Third Amendment Directions on June 24. The new rules will cover electronic banking transactions by bank customers from Jan. 1, 2027, pushing back the start by six months compared to the July 1 timeline in the March draft.

Individuals and sole proprietors hit by eligible small-value fraudulent electronic banking transactions can recover 85% of their net loss or up to ₹25,000, whichever is less, but only once in their lifetime. The total loss must not exceed ₹50,000. Victims have five calendar days to report the fraud to both their bank and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal or Helpline 1930.

The headline payout puts more on banks, but the formula leans on the RBI. For frauds in India under ₹29,412, the RBI covers 65% of the loss, customer’s bank pays 10%, and beneficiary bank pays 10%. That leaves the RBI picking up about 76.5% of total compensation. If the loss is between ₹29,412 and ₹50,000, the total payout maxes out at ₹25,000, split up as ₹19,118 from the RBI and ₹2,941 each from the two banks.

Cross-border cases can leave the customer’s bank handling more because there isn’t always an Indian beneficiary bank to charge. Where there’s a cap, the customer’s bank puts up ₹5,882, around 23.5% of the payout, and the RBI covers ₹19,118.

RBI split out zero-liability cases on their own. If fraud is the bank’s fault, customers get a full reversal no matter when they report. Customers also get full reversal if they report a third-party breach within five days. For cases involving customer negligence, the small-value compensation only covers the loss that isn’t otherwise protected.

Credit-card issuers are on a tighter timeline. The RBI directed banks to give a shadow reversal, or provisional credit, for fraudulent credit-card electronic banking transactions within five calendar days after customers notify them. Customers can’t spend the shadow amount, but they won’t get hit with extra interest or charges during the review.

Banks have to resolve domestic fraudulent transaction complaints in 45 days, with 60 days for cross-border ones. They need to send instant SMS alerts for electronic banking transactions over ₹500, and email alerts if an email is registered. Lenders also have to provide 24×7 reporting, through phone banking, SMS, email, IVR, toll-free numbers or at branches.

The investor question is real. Per case, direct reimbursement is a minor cost for big banks, but the new rule means higher outlay on fraud systems, alerts, more call-centre staff, and stronger audit trails. Final RBI guidance tells banks to give regular fraud complaint reports to their board or a board-level panel, showing case numbers, total value and type for card-present, card-not-present, internet, mobile, and ATM transactions.

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra described the proposal in February as support for small customers. “We will compensate them as long as it is unintended,” he told reporters after the policy meeting, according to Reuters. Nearly 65% of bank fraud cases reported involve losses under ₹50,000, he said. “The amount is very small for us,” Malhotra said, “but for small customers” it helps right away. Reuters

The rule is temporary. Banks have to pay compensation for losses on fraudulent electronic banking transactions that take place within one year from when the directions start. Banks are also required to keep records for two years after the closure of the mechanism, for audit, supervision and review purposes.

Indian stocks were closed on Friday with both NSE and BSE shut for Muharram. Markets will start up again Monday, June 29. Bank stocks will see their first normal local session since the RBI’s final notice and reports focusing on the five-day credit-card shadow reversals.

data.title: Larsen & Toubro (NSE:LT) Gets a Moody’s Upgrade But Shares Slip
data.description:
Mumbai, July 10, 2026, 01:34 IST

Larsen & Toubro Limited (NSE:LT) dropped for a third day on Thursday, settling at ₹3,886.00 on the NSE. India’s main indexes were higher, but L&T lagged. The daily move was minor. Moody’s latest rating got a nod from investors as a credit positive, but no one’s calling it a fix for execution risk.

The gap between bond optimism and equity caution is in focus now. L&T just secured an improved global credit rating and announced a tech tie-up for government AI projects, but the stock trades about 12.5% under its Feb. 24 peak of ₹4,440.00. Traders seem unimpressed by the better balance sheet, zeroing in instead on whether L&T can translate its big international order book into profits while West Asia remains volatile.

India stocks picked up on Thursday after Wednesday’s drop. The Nifty 50 ended up 0.34% at 23,962.80, and the Sensex climbed 0.31% to 76,741.82. Aamar Deo Singh of Angel One said investors are “positioning for the results season.” He also said Middle East worries “are likely to persist.” Reuters

L&T’s drop this week has outpaced the Nifty. Shares are down 3.8% since Monday’s close, compared with a 1.9% slip in the index, based on historical price data. Volume hit 5.12 million shares on Thursday, higher than both previous sessions’ combined.

Moody’s gave L&T a Baa1 long-term issuer rating with a stable outlook. The investment-grade Baa1 rating signals Moody’s sees decent capacity to meet debt. L&T noted the rating stands two levels above India’s Baa3. Moody’s also put a Baa1 on L&T Hydrocarbon Saudi Company, showing West Asia’s continued weight for the group.

There was also a growth play in the last 48 hours. L&T Vyoma, the AI cloud and digital infrastructure arm of L&T, said it will team up with Fortanix and NVIDIA Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA) for confidential computing. The technology protects data during processing, not just when stored or in transit. L&T Vyoma managing director Prashant Chiranjive Jain said India needs “sovereign infrastructure and secure AI capabilities.” Larsen & Toubro

West Asia is both a big source of orders and a risk for L&T. Around 40% of L&T’s $77.82 billion order backlog is tied to the Middle East, according to a Reuters report from May. That’s work the company has won but hasn’t done yet. L&T has guided for 10%-12% revenue growth this fiscal year. Emkay Research has moved its rating to “Add” from “Buy”, and HSBC analysts have pointed to geopolitical risks possibly slowing expansion and market share. Reuters

Valuation is tight for any weak results. Economic Times puts L&T’s market cap near ₹5.35 trillion, with a P/E ratio at 33.29 and a P/B at 4.17. P/E shows what investors pay for earnings, P/B for book value. Those are premium numbers, not for a struggling contractor. L&T needs its order book to turn into sales without losing too much on margins.

Some peers showed buyers sticking around for select engineering and construction stocks. Siemens Limited (NSE:SIEMENS) and KEC International Limited (NSE:KEC) ended higher, while NCC Limited (NSE:NCC) lost ground. L&T traded between the two, but its three-day slide stood out to investors.

For the open on Friday, traders will be watching Thursday’s NSE low at ₹3,867.80. If shares fall below that, the drop stretches into a fourth day. Any bounce would need clear signs on execution, West Asia deadlines and margin numbers. Moody’s gave some support for credit, but equity investors remain cautious, still looking for evidence.

data.title: Cupid Limited shares rebound, but sales numbers get focus
data.description:
Mumbai, July 9, 2026, 23:31 IST

Cupid Limited (NSE:CUPID) bounced back on Thursday, closing up 6.61% at ₹210.01 on the NSE. That followed a 10.91% drop the previous session. Traders came back into the small-cap contraceptive name after management raised its revenue forecast. The stock moved between ₹196.00 and ₹216.86, almost an 11% swing, with volume at 104.27 million shares.

The timing is important because this is no longer a single-day jump. Cupid said June-quarter revenue should top ₹150 crore and lifted its FY27 revenue view to over ₹660 crore from ₹600 crore. Chairman and MD Aditya Kumar Halwasiya said the company’s “multiple growth engines” are starting to scale up together.

Investors have piled in, leaving Cupid trading at a high price. Based on Sharekhan’s closing market cap of ₹28,239.22 crore, the stock now sits at 42.8 times its FY27 sales goal. That price-to-sales ratio, calculated as market cap over expected revenue, offers little cushion if sales slip.

Indian benchmarks edged higher Thursday, with the Nifty 50 up 0.34% and Sensex up 0.31%. Small-cap stocks bounced 1.8% after a steep dip Wednesday linked to jitters over the Middle East. Cupid’s stock easily outpaced those gains, posting a much larger jump than the rest of the market.

The math explains why this stock is behaving more like a guidance play than a regular earnings name:

Cupid’s audited customer base moved sharply. Full-year revenue from operations for FY26 was ₹357.71 crore, up from ₹183.52 crore last year. Net profit jumped to ₹108.23 crore compared with ₹40.89 crore. The company signaled over ₹150 crore for the June quarter, around 25% higher than the March quarter’s ₹119.96 crore.

Cupid is telling investors it’s not just a condom producer anymore. On its website, the company lists male and female condoms, water-based lubricants and IVD products, which are medical tests on samples outside the body. The company says it has WHO/UNFPA prequalification and exports to over 100 countries.

Technical analysts dialed back their tone on the speed of the rally. Hitesh Tailor at Choice Broking said Cupid still sits in a “higher high–higher low” setup, with its chart seeing fresh peaks and troughs. Virat Jagad from Bonanza pointed to the ₹195-₹200 range as key support after profit-taking came in near ₹220. The Economic Times

Peer comparisons have limits, making it tough to find a clear anchor for Cupid’s rerating. Mankind Pharma (NSE:MANKIND) owns Manforce, which it calls India’s leading condom brand, but that unit is only part of a bigger pharma and consumer-health business. TTK Healthcare (NSE:TTKHLTCARE) sells Skore condoms, but it’s also a broad healthcare and consumer-products player.

The risk now sits squarely in the multiple. After Thursday, Cupid’s trailing PE was over 240x, market data show. Any holdup in the tender, squeezed margins, currency moves, or a miss on brand sales could make that high valuation work the other way. Next up is the June-quarter report—watch if the full numbers match the early sales and show margins strong enough to back up the rally before audited results land.

data.title: Kalyan Jewellers Stock Rallies 18% on Q1 Numbers
data.description:
Kalyan Jewellers shares shot up 18% after the company posted its Q1 update.

Kalyan Jewellers India shot up 18.4% Thursday to end at 443 rupees on the NSE. Shares turned around hard after the company’s Q1 business update.

It was a big move, even with Indian stocks trading higher. The Nifty 50 gained 0.34% to 23,962.80 and the BSE Sensex was up 0.31% at 76,741.82. Investors bought back into some mid- and small-cap shares after a selloff on Wednesday. Reuters quoted Aamar Deo Singh, senior vice president at Angel One, saying investors saw “strong growth” from banks, consumer goods and jewellery companies and were getting ready for results season. Reuters

Kalyan bounced after a rough open to the week. Shares slipped Tuesday, even with good operating numbers, then climbed on Wednesday. The gains sped up Thursday as investors looked again at the June-quarter growth.

Kalyan’s 52-week range is between 327.05 rupees and 617.70 rupees, according to Moneycontrol. Even after Thursday’s big move, the stock is trading well below its high. The BSE quote showed 444.55 rupees, up 18.75%, at 4:01 p.m. local time.

The company reported in a July 7 exchange filing that consolidated revenue rose roughly 38% year over year for the quarter ended June 30. It said India business was up more than 38%. Same-store sales increased about 28%.

The quarter saw a test of demand. Kalyan said this year’s 28-day Adhik Maas month, which comes once every three years and tends to slow wedding-related buying in parts of India, landed entirely in the quarter. That put more investor focus on India growth.

Kalyan said recycled gold made up more than 46% of revenue last quarter, and the share was above 55% in June after the “Shine with India” campaign. The company said this higher recycled content came from gold customers brought back and Kalyan put back into its supply chain.

International business rose around 35%, with the Middle East up roughly 30%, though April saw slower footfall tied to regional tensions. International sales made up about 14% of total revenue. Candere, Kalyan’s digital-first jewelry play, was up about 112%. Kalyan added 12 new showrooms and opened five more Candere locations in India this quarter, bringing the total to 524 stores at June 30.

Peers have shown solid read-across, but the numbers aren’t really apples to apples since each firm reports with its own business mix.

Titan, owner of Tanishq and Mia, posted 39% growth in its domestic jewellery business and 41% in its overall consumer business for the June quarter. Reuters said the update pointed to steady discretionary spending in India, even as gold prices stayed high and urban demand was mixed. Reuters Senco Gold shares gained after the company logged 60% revenue growth in its Q1 business update, the Economic Times reported.

Broker calls gave a boost. Business Standard said Motilal Oswal Financial Services kept its “Buy” rating on Kalyan Jewellers, stuck with a 525 rupee target after the quarterly update, and pointed to the gold recirculation campaign lifting recycled-gold’s share and cutting reliance on imported gold. Business Standard

There’s a risk Thursday’s rally baked in some of the upside before the final numbers are out. Kalyan said its reported metrics are only through limited review and full profit, margin and working-capital figures aren’t coming until the board signs off on results. The company’s overseas operations still face watch points from Middle East tensions. Angel One’s Singh told Reuters that while some volatility got priced in after Wednesday’s drop, “some concerns are likely to persist.”

data.title: HDFC Bank’s recovery leaves deposit trouble on the table
data.description:
Mumbai, July 9, 2026, 22:35 IST

  • HDFC Bank gained 0.9% Thursday, outpacing the Sensex and Nifty following Wednesday’s selloff.
  • The stock action is now less about loan growth and more about funding quality. CASA deposits fell from March as term deposits increased.
  • Investors will see this month if June-quarter results show stronger loan growth has hurt margins.

HDFC Bank Limited (NSE:HDFCBANK) added Thursday, although the gain didn’t answer a key investor concern. India’s top private bank has picked up the pace on loan growth, but is leaning harder on higher-cost deposits to support it.

The stock finished up 0.89% at ₹817.70 on the BSE, beating the BSE Sensex (INDEXBOM:SENSEX), which added 0.31% to 76,741.82, and the Nifty 50 (INDEXNSE:NIFTY_50), which rose 0.34% to 23,962.80. But shares still closed 19.86% under the 52-week high, according to MarketWatch, showing the June-quarter update hasn’t yet sparked a full recovery.

Kotak Mahindra Bank (NSE:KOTAKBANK) climbed above HDFC Bank on Thursday. ICICI Bank (NSE:ICICIBANK) was little changed and Axis Bank (NSE:AXISBANK) slipped. HDFC still posted a solid gain but didn’t pull ahead of the group.

The mix is in focus now, more than just the headline size. HDFC Bank’s July 4 filing showed period-end gross advances at ₹30.61 trillion as of June 30, up 15.4% from a year ago. Period-end deposits climbed 14.7% to ₹31.705 trillion. Growth is solid. But the period-end credit-deposit ratio—loans against deposits—hit about 96.5%, up from 95.3% at the end of March.

CASA deposits, the current and savings accounts that are often a lower-cost funding source for banks, dropped 3.3% from March. Time deposits climbed 4.9%. The period-end CASA ratio slid to about 32.3%, down from 34.1% at the end of March, according to the bank’s numbers. Investors look at this, as relying on more expensive deposits can pressure net interest margin—the difference between what banks make on loans and what they pay for funding.

Motilal Oswal Financial Services said HDFC’s loan growth beat estimates by a small margin and deposit growth matched forecasts. The firm expects HDFC’s margins to edge down for the quarter, with a 2-basis-point drop from the previous period. A basis point equals one-hundredth of a percent.

Indian stocks bounced back after dropping 2% Wednesday, as the wider market gave support. Investors are focusing on upcoming first-quarter earnings while keeping an eye on Middle East tensions. Aamar Deo Singh, senior vice-president at Angel One (NSE:ANGELONE), told Reuters investors are “positioning for the results season,” noting pre-earnings updates from banks, consumer firms and jewellers have helped. But Singh said concerns over geopolitics are likely to stay. Reuters

Banks that posted stronger loan growth got the first boost earlier this week. HDFC Bank, IndusInd Bank and Bandhan Bank all reported above-forecast loan growth, while Kotak’s growth slowed, Jefferies analysts said, according to Moneycontrol. Piran Engineer at CLSA told Reuters most banks matched or beat forecasts, “with the exception of Kotak and RBL,” but flagged that loan-book details and lower CASA ratios still need attention. Moneycontrol

There’s a chance Thursday’s gain is just a relief rally rather than a sign of a new valuation. If HDFC’s June-quarter numbers show higher loan growth but weaker margins—or if the drop in low-cost deposits carries on—investors may question the quality of growth. Shares still trade about 20% below the 52-week high, so the bank has more to prove.

HDFC Bank is up next with its board set to meet on July 18 for June-quarter results, both standalone and consolidated. A Thursday update from the company pointed to the upcoming earnings call. Beyond headline profit, investors will be watching how much it costs for the bank to fund its loan growth.

data.title: Eternal falls; Blinkit trade fuels 34% price call
data.description:
MUMBAI, July 9, 2026, 01:38 IST

  • Eternal ended down 0.93% at ₹286.70 on Wednesday. Volume came in at 58.56 million shares.
  • Motilal Oswal is sticking with its Buy rating and a ₹380 target, pointing to 34% upside.
  • Indian stocks were closed at the deadline and set to reopen at 09:15 IST.

Eternal Ltd. lost ground Wednesday, but outperformed the wider market after Motilal Oswal put out a new note saying the Blinkit owner still has more room to run, even as the quick commerce and food delivery space gets more crowded.

Shares closed down 0.93% at ₹286.70 on the NSE. The stock moved between ₹283.75 and ₹296.55 through the session. Volume jumped to 58.56 million shares, up from 45.31 million on Tuesday, according to Investing.com market data.

Indian stocks were already having a tough day, with the Nifty 50 down 2.12% and the Sensex off 2.15%. That’s the steepest drop in over three months. Oil prices jumped, hurting sentiment for India, which imports most of its crude. NSE’s main equity market is open from 09:15 to 15:30 IST.

Eternal, which used to be Zomato, trades less like a food-delivery stock now and more like a play on Blinkit, the quick-commerce arm bringing groceries and other items in minutes. The group’s listed businesses are Zomato, Blinkit, District, and Hyperpure.

Motilal Oswal’s Abhishek Pathak and Keval Bhagat said in a July 6 note that Blinkit’s current valuation prices in an “EV/EBITDA multiple of just 24x” on FY29 numbers. EV/EBITDA is a way to compare a firm’s overall value to operating earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.

The broker stuck with its Buy call and a ₹380 target, calling for 34% potential upside. Food delivery is a steady duopoly with Swiggy, it said. Quick-commerce growth is slowing but the broker sees profit potential improving as more stores mature.

That makes Swiggy the direct comp in this case. Motilal’s model puts a higher multiple on Eternal’s food delivery than Swiggy’s, and assigns Blinkit a positive implied quick-commerce value, while Swiggy’s Instamart lands with a negative one in the model’s table.

Eternal’s most recent quarter kept some bulls in the game. The company posted a 186% jump in Q4FY26 consolidated adjusted revenue to ₹17,680 crore. B2C net order value was ₹26,880 crore, up 54%. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 160% to ₹429 crore.

Blinkit drove the numbers. The company reported NOV up 95.4% year-over-year in Q4FY26, 216 net new stores, and adjusted EBITDA at ₹37 crore, or 0.3% of NOV, Upstox reported. Group CEO Albinder Dhindsa said quick commerce “still had a long way to go before it becomes a zero sum game.” Upstox – Online Stock and Share Trading

The market is pricing in strong execution, leaving little margin for error. If competitors cut prices, order growth slows, delivery costs go up or consumer demand drops, Blinkit’s unit economics could come under pressure. Higher oil prices and foreign selling are risks across the board. Kranti Bathini of Wealthmills Securities told Reuters that the oil shock might spark “fresh foreign outflows.” Reuters

Traders on Thursday will look at whether Eternal holds the ₹280–₹290 area after the broad selloff on Wednesday. The stock trades well under its 52-week high of ₹368.45, and sits roughly 35% above its 52-week low of ₹212.60. Moves could still be sharp, with crude, flows, and any fresh details on Blinkit’s margins in focus.

data.title: Eternal (NSE:ETERNAL) trading beats Swiggy, Blinkit scale holds up quick-commerce flows

MUMBAI, July 3, 2026, 04:31 (IST)

  • Eternal ended July 2 at ₹279.70 after hitting a high of ₹285.95. Trading volume stood at 4.13 crore shares and turnover came in at ₹1,155 crore.

  • No trades had gone through at the time of the report; regular equity trading on the NSE is scheduled from 09:15 to 15:30 IST.

Eternal Limited (NSE:ETERNAL) closed unchanged at ₹279.70 on Thursday. Turnover was heavy at ₹1,155.20 crore with 4.13 crore shares changing hands. The stock saw lots of trading but ended flat.

It makes more sense to stack up Eternal against Swiggy, not the Nifty. Swiggy ended at ₹249, up 0.81%. Volume was 1.07 crore shares and turnover was ₹267.19 crore. Eternal closed with a ₹2,69,920 crore market cap, while Swiggy’s stood at ₹68,732 crore.

The market focus is sticking to Blinkit. Eternal owns Zomato, Blinkit, District and Hyperpure. Founder Deepinder Goyal said during the rebrand that they’d use the Eternal name in public once something besides Zomato took the lead. “Today, with Blinkit, I feel we are here,” he said at the time. Reuters

Laxmikant Shukla, technical research analyst at YES Securities, told Business Today that the stock could enter a short-term consolidation following the sharp jump. He sees better risk-reward for those buying dips toward ₹268-₹270. If the price holds above ₹280, the odds increase for a push to ₹300, while support sits at ₹255.

Eternal closed higher but the move wasn’t all about the broader market. India’s Nifty 50 added 0.71% at 24,175.7 and the Sensex advanced 0.75% to 77,502.12 on Thursday. Local stocks found support as oil prices slipped and IT shares rallied. G. Chokkalingam at Equinomics Research told Reuters oil’s drop was “the single biggest factor for India” with impacts on growth, inflation, reserves and the fiscal deficit. Reuters

No new operating trigger showed up in the latest exchange filings from the company. Moneycontrol listed a July 1 stock options grant and a June 19 trading-window closure ahead of June-quarter results as the recent exchange items. Last earnings, reported April 28, showed Eternal with Q4 FY26 consolidated adjusted revenue up 186% year on year to ₹17,680 crore, B2C net order value up 54% to ₹26,880 crore, and adjusted EBITDA up 160% to ₹429 crore.

Quick commerce is pulling capital from Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), Walmart Inc’s (NYSE:WMT) Flipkart, Reliance Industries Ltd’s (NSE:RELIANCE) JioMart and Zepto, just as investors are pricing Eternal based on Blinkit’s scale. If Blinkit’s June-quarter update shows strong order density without bigger discounts, Thursday’s active but flat trade could be seen as accumulation. If expanding stores needs extra subsidy, that same pattern will look more like buyers holding back.

data.title: BSE stock drops ahead of NSE IPO review
data.description:
BSE shares slipped in Mumbai trade as the NSE IPO valuation test comes up. Mumbai, July 3, 2026, 02:41 IST

  • BSE Ltd dropped 2.78% Thursday, lagging the Sensex, which gained 0.75%. The exchange is now down about 3.5 percentage points against the index.
  • Shares have gained 39.32% in the past year and 34.48% in three months, though the stock trades nearly 14% under its 52-week high.
  • NSE’s upcoming IPO gives investors a clearer benchmark to compare BSE’s valuation premium.
  • More BSE-linked indexes have hit the market, boosting the passive product lineup, but the bulk of earnings still comes from derivatives fees.

Equities hadn’t opened for trading as of the dateline. Indian equities are usually open from 09:15 to 15:30 IST, meaning the last available price for BSE Ltd (NSE:BSE) is from Thursday’s close.

BSE slipped to settle at 3,834.70 rupees on the NSE, dropping 109.41 rupees, or 2.78%, from the last close. Trading volume hit 3.43 million shares. Shares started up at 3,963.70 rupees, ran up to 3,970.20, but then fell back to a low of 3,820 rupees.

BSE lagged even as the rest of the market was up. The BSE Sensex moved up 0.75% to 77,502.12 and the Nifty 50 added 0.71% to 24,175.70, with gains in IT stocks and falling crude prices helping. BSE trailed the Sensex by roughly 3.53 percentage points for the session.

BSE kept its longer-term premium, with a one-year return of 39.32% and a three-month return of 34.48%. Market cap was around 1.56 trillion rupees at Thursday’s close.

The bigger question for holders is the looming valuation review from National Stock Exchange of India. NSE is expected to price at about 5 trillion rupees, which comes to around 3.2 times the latest value of BSE. NSE’s FY26 profit after tax was about 4.1 times BSE’s, too. That difference is why the IPO might change how investors are valuing Indian exchange stocks.

Centrum Broking vice president Mohit Mangal said NSE, with a 5 trillion rupee market cap, trades at 36x FY28 earnings. That’s at a 15%-20% discount versus the BSE valuation. Reuters has said NSE’s IPO will likely be a pure offer-for-sale, covering about 6% of its equity and could be valued around $3.3 billion.

BSE is still counting on derivatives for its bull case. The FY26 investor deck shows average daily notional turnover in equity derivatives up to 245 trillion rupees in Q4 FY26 from 131 trillion in Q1 FY26. Daily lots traded climbed to 151 million from 82 million in that period.

PL Capital’s Shreya Khandelwal, Dhanik Hegde and Harshada Gite launched coverage on BSE, putting a “BUY” on the stock with a target of 4,850 rupees. The analysts said BSE’s index options premium market share went from zero in FY23 to around 28% in FY26. They see operating revenue growing close to 25% a year over FY26-FY28.

Concentration is the issue here. PL’s report put BSE’s FY26 operating revenue at 79% from transaction income. So options trading, regulatory changes, and expiry-day rules matter more to BSE than to peers with broader fee streams.

BSE Index Services on Wednesday rolled out the BSE REITs and Commercial Real Estate Index, with a base value of 1,000 and first value date of September 2022. The index will reconstitute semi-annually, in March and September, and caps any single name at 20%. Ashutosh Singh, MD and CEO of BSE Index Services, said the index is meant to offer “focused exposure” to India’s yield-generating real estate market. The Economic Times

Mirae Asset Investment Managers has rolled out the Mirae Asset BSE Midcap 150 Momentum 30 ETF and a fund of fund. The ETF tracks the BSE Midcap 150 Momentum 30 Total Return Index. Subscriptions start July 6. Siddharth Srivastava, ETF products head and fund manager at Mirae Asset, said momentum strategies often work when the market moves in a clear direction.

BSE board has proposed a final dividend of 10 rupees a share, pending approval from shareholders. The record date is July 10. The company said in a May filing the payout will be made on or before September 17. At Thursday’s close, the dividend works out to roughly 0.26% of the share price.

data.title: TCS share price jumps 4.3% but stock still sits near 52-week low before July 9 results
data.description:
BENGALURU, July 3, 2026, 03:33 IST

  • Tata Consultancy Services Limited (NSE:TCS) closed at ₹2,068.10 on Thursday, up 4.3%, as the Nifty IT index rose 4.64%.
  • The stock recovered about 74% of its prior two-session fall, but stayed 40.7% below its 52-week high.
  • TCS will report Q1FY27 results on July 9; the board will also consider an interim dividend with July 15 as record date if declared.
  • At the dateline time, Indian cash equities were outside NSE’s regular 09:15-15:30 IST session; latest prices are Thursday closes.

At the dateline time, Indian cash equities were between sessions. The latest trade for Tata Consultancy Services Limited (NSE:TCS) was Thursday’s close: ₹2,068.10, up 4.3%, after an open at ₹2,008.00 and an intraday low at ₹2,002.50. Volume was 6.04 million shares.

The cleaner read is in the repair trade. TCS lost ₹115.30 over June 30 and July 1, then gained ₹85.50 on Thursday. That recovered 74.2% of the two-session fall, but left the stock 1.4% below Monday’s close of ₹2,097.90.

For investors, the split matters. The stock bounced hard, but it was still just 4.6% above its 52-week low of ₹1,976.80 and 40.7% below its 52-week high of ₹3,489.90. ET data put TCS’s market value at ₹748,257 crore, with a PE ratio of 14.58 and PB ratio of 6.62.

The stock move beat the broad market but did not beat the sector. Nifty IT rose 4.64% to 26,965.05. Reuters said the IT index led sector gains after a 6.5% slide over four losing sessions. The Nifty 50 rose 0.71% to 24,175.70 and the BSE Sensex gained 0.75% to 77,502.12.

Infosys Limited (NSE:INFY) gained 5.6% on Thursday, ahead of TCS’s 4.3% rise, Reuters reported. HCL Technologies Limited (NSE:HCLTECH) rose 4.12% to ₹1,077.50, while Wipro Limited (NSE:WIPRO) gained 2.35% to ₹174.05, according to MarketWatch data.

Oil gave Indian equities cover from the global tech selloff. “The drop in oil prices is also supporting the momentum towards India,” said G. Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at Equinomics Research. V.K. Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments, said lower crude would strengthen India’s macros and help growth while keeping inflation in check. Reuters

The harder question for TCS is still growth. Reuters reported on June 19 that India’s Nifty IT index had fallen to a three-year low after Accenture PLC (NYSE:ACN) cut its annual revenue outlook and flagged softer managed-services bookings. Indian IT stocks had slid about 29% so far in 2026 at that point, against an 8.3% drop in the Nifty 50.

Hiren Dasani, chief investment officer for emerging markets at WhiteOak Capital, told Reuters in February: “Nobody can say with confidence where IT business models will land.” Mayuresh Joshi, head of equity research at William O’Neil & Co, said the market was looking for growth, which was “clearly missing.” Reuters

That puts July 9 ahead of the dividend line. TCS said its board will approve audited standalone and consolidated interim results for the quarter ended June 30 and consider an interim dividend. If declared, the record date is July 15.

TCS’s investor page lists FY26 revenue down 2.4% in constant currency, an operating margin of 25%, a $40.7 billion order book and annualized AI revenue above $2.3 billion in Q4FY26. Those numbers set the base for the June-quarter read on whether Thursday’s stock bounce has earnings support.

The company’s trading window has been shut since June 23 and will stay shut until 48 hours after the results are made public, TCS said in its exchange filing.

data.title: EPF Scheme 2026 fixes ₹1,800 monthly PF limit; 17-year tenure stays crucial for investors
data.description:
NEW DELHI, July 2, 2026, 20:34 IST

  • India rolled out its new EPF Scheme on June 29, replacing the old 1952 plan.
  • PF stays at 12% each for workers and companies, with payments tied to the wage ceiling cap.
  • Investors aren’t as focused on the one-time enrolment plan for workers who’ve been excluded since April 2009.
  • When PF isn’t deducted from workers, most of the financial risk lands on employers rather than on employees.

India’s new provident fund rules have put a spotlight on two numbers for investors in labour-heavy companies: ₹1,800, which is now the standard monthly PF payment per side under the wage ceiling, and April 1, 2009, the new cut-off for a fresh enrolment period. The window lets firms fix any past gaps in coverage for older staff. The government notified the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 2026 on June 29 under the Code on Social Security, 2020.

NSE equity trading did not open at the deadline. The exchange lists regular trading from 09:15 to 15:30 IST.

The Gazette reported the Employees’ Enrolment Campaign, 2026, is open until Oct. 31, 2026. Companies are allowed to enroll staff hired from April 1, 2009, through March 31, 2026, as long as they’re still on payroll when declared and haven’t been previously registered.

This matters for sectors like staffing, construction, retail and facility management where headcounts run high, because payrolls go through both contractors and main firms. Under this setup, the employer puts up both the employer and employee shares at once for workers on their own rolls or, in some cases, hired through a contractor.

The personal-finance angle is simple. The contribution rate stays at 12% of wages from both sides, but some notified establishments still use the 10% rate. Business Standard said the employee share is locked to the ₹15,000 statutory cap, so it comes out to ₹1,800 a month—any extra is voluntary.

The table skips the auto savings number. Instead, it gives the gap between the legal minimum and a full PF wage rule. India Today reports that employers match voluntary contributions above ₹1,800 only if the contract or company policy requires it.

Business Standard reported that workers paying the full PF on their actual salary likely won’t notice any difference in their pay-slips. There’s no automatic cut for those already contributing on real pay. Any sums above the cap can still go in as voluntary PF, if workers or employers choose, under the rules that stand now.

Puneet Gupta, Partner at EY India’s People Advisory Services, called the scheme an “important step toward implementing the labour codes” in comments to ANI. Gupta said companies face “enhanced governance and compliance obligations” now, including contractor compliance, ownership disclosure, more electronic filings, and dealing with exempted PF trusts. The Economic Times

Withdrawal rules mean more paperwork for admins. NewsOnAir said the scheme will change partial withdrawal terms covering medical expenses, education fees, marriage, and housing, setting a minimum balance and new requirements. Business Standard reported the list of withdrawal reasons will go from 13 down to three key categories.

PF, pension and insurance claims now have to be processed in 20 days under new rules, Upstox reported. If there’s an unjustified delay, the rules allow for a 12% annual penal interest. The penalty can be deducted from the Commissioner’s salary.

data.title: GE Vernova T&D India’s ₹1.27 lakh crore market cap raises questions on order-book premium
data.description:
BENGALURU, June 30, 2026, 02:32 IST

  • GE Vernova T&D India (NSE:GVT&D) ended Monday at ₹4,956.50, dropping 1.72%. Nifty 50 slipped 0.46% the same day.
  • The stock is trading at roughly 5.9x its March order backlog and 20.5x FY26 revenue, going by company filings and Monday’s market cap.
  • The ₹550 million capacity plan looks small compared to the market cap, but it shows the real test now is turning the backlog into actual supply and holding on to margins.

Indian stocks were closed at the cutoff. The National Stock Exchange’s regular cash session goes from 9:15 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. IST, so the last price for GE Vernova T&D India Limited (NSE:GVT&D) is Monday’s close.

The stock closed Monday at ₹4,956.50, off ₹86.50 or 1.72%. Shares traded between ₹5,079 and ₹4,721.50, a 7.1% move from the last close at ₹5,043. Weak finish for the stock, but it climbed about 5% off the session low.

It’s not the order book that’s holding the stock back. It’s what was paid to get it. GE Vernova T&D posted Q4 order bookings at ₹86.1 billion and put its order backlog at ₹214.6 billion as of March 2026. For FY26, revenue came in at ₹62.06 billion, with net profit at ₹12.33 billion.

This matters as a strong backlog-to-sales ratio helps support revenue, but it also puts pressure on execution. Orders need to move to billings fast enough to keep up the valuation. Cash conversion is also key. Operating cash flow for FY26 was ₹17.10 billion, compared to net profit of ₹12.33 billion.

Chief Executive Sandeep Zanzaria told analysts on the May earnings call that the order book stayed strong in Q4. The company reported ₹86.1 billion in Q4 bookings, a jump of 188% from last year.

The board cleared ₹550 million to boost capacity for disconnectors and drives for 362 kV dead tank circuit breakers at Vallam, Tamil Nadu. First production is expected by December 2026. Funding comes from internal accruals, according to the company.

The peer group moved in both directions on Monday, so the drop in GE Vernova T&D wasn’t just about the sector. Hitachi Energy India (NSE:POWERINDIA) climbed 2.97%, ABB India (NSE:ABB) was up 1.93%, while Siemens Energy India (NSE:ENRIN) slipped 2.76%.

The long run-up in the chart still means the stock has little margin for error. NSE figures show GE Vernova T&D has climbed 59.58% in 2026 to date and 115.21% in the past year, while Nifty 50 gained 11.63% and 9.56%. Over three years, GE Vernova T&D is up 2,266.45%, versus the index’s 63.61%.

Jefferies began covering GE Vernova T&D last week with a Hold and a ₹6,000 price target. The firm kept Buy on Hitachi Energy India and Siemens Energy India, saying those two offer clearer earnings growth in India’s power transmission story.

Indian shares dropped Monday, snapping a three-week rally. The Nifty 50 lost 0.46% and the Sensex gave up 0.48%. Saurabh Jain at SMC Global told Reuters “fresh upside is limited” as traders watch monsoon progress after weak June rain. Reuters
